elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New sentence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed..." — symmetrical, applies to PB and SFJ alike.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap is a single basis — "the amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under Article 6 in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim" — with no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor; the drafter expressly declined to propose it.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained first sentence of 15.11: "NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES..."

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Cap opens "Except for ... each Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The exception list covers indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence/willful misconduct and SFJ's Article 4 funding only; no data protection or security carve-out appears anywhere in the rendered text.
"Except for each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 12..."
"...each Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct..." sits outside the cap.
"...each Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct..." is an express exception to the cap.
No fraud carve-out in the exception list; the drafter states it was not volunteered.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the exception list; expressly left open in the rationale.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Savings sentence extended: "...AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2, OR ANY OTHER PB PAYMENT OBLIGATION, WHICH ARE NOT "DAMAGES" SUBJECT TO ANY CAP." — covers PB payment obligations as a whole, not a narrow subset.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... will not exceed ..." — one cap binding both PB and SFJ; no residual unlimited-Customer language remains.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Cap = "the amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under Article 6 in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim"; Article 6 is the sole PB-to-SFJ consideration stream in an agreement with no defined "Fees", so the twelve-month fee-equivalent basis is satisfied (see reasons for the zero-lookback risk).
"Except for each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 12..." — indemnities sit outside the cap for both Parties.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "...each Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10..." is excepted from the cap.
Gross negligence expressly listed among the exceptions to the aggregate cap.
Willful misconduct expressly listed among the exceptions to the aggregate cap.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the inserted sentence creates a single mutual aggregate cap on a twelve-month lookback of the only PB-to-SFJ payment stream (Article 6) and carves out indemnification (Art. 12), confidentiality (Art. 10), gross negligence and willful misconduct.

Preferred level fails on four elements: no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, and no carve-outs for data protection/security breaches, fraud, or infringement of the other Party's intellectual property. To reach preferred, amend the cap to "the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000" and add "each Party's breach of its data protection or security obligations, its fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights" to the exception list.

Minimality fails (extra 1): the carve-out for "SFJ's obligation to pay or incur Development Costs under Article 4" is not required by any element of the chosen fallback checklist. It is an additional substantive requirement imported into the cap sentence; delete it, or move the point to a separate negotiated ask, if the proposal is to stay at the fallback.

Minimality fails (extra 2): extending the retained savings sentence from "AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2" to "OR ANY OTHER PB PAYMENT OBLIGATION, WHICH ARE NOT "DAMAGES" SUBJECT TO ANY CAP" implements a preferred-level element (Customer payment obligations excluded from damages) that is outside the fallback checklist; the existing sentence already shields the Article 6 and 14.2 amounts from Section 15.11, so the expansion is not needed to make the fallback cap workable.

Substantive warning on the cap basis (not an element failure, but repair recommended): Article 6 payments are event/approval-driven, so in many twelve-month windows the lookback amount may be nil, producing a near-zero cap that principally cuts down PB's recovery against SFJ for uncarved breaches. Adding the preferred USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor cures this and simultaneously advances the preferred level.

Intent is preserved: the mutual indirect/consequential waiver, the deemed-consequential list (speculative sales, unachieved Article 6 events, contingent payments), the failure-of-essential-purpose sentence and all cross-references (Articles 4, 6, 10, 12; Section 14.2) survive intact, and the new cap does not contradict any retained sentence or leave a dangling term.
